faqs.a: Middle C is C4 at 261.63 Hz. On this keyboard it is the first white key on the left. On a real piano, it sits near the centre, usually under the brand logo, at the boundary between the bass and treble sections.

White keys play the natural notes A through G, and black keys play the sharps and flats between them. Each octave has 7 white and 5 black keys in the same repeating pattern: groups of two, then groups of three.
faqs.q: Why are piano keys black and white?

faqs.a: Associate each note with a landmark: C sits just left of the two-black-key group, F just left of the three-black-key group. Start by finding all the Cs, then learn D (between the two blacks) and work outward. The quiz mode here drills exactly this.
faqs.q: How do I memorise which key is which note?

faqs.a: Start with just the white keys (C to B) until you score above 80%, then include the black keys. Use the replay button freely - hearing the note several times before answering builds the memory faster than guessing.
faqs.q: How should I practise with the quiz?

faqs.a: It tests pitch recognition by ear, which is the foundation of playing by ear, transcribing songs, and singing in tune. Interval and chord drills in the ear-training tool are the natural next step once single notes feel easy.
faqs.q: What does note identification actually train?

faqs.a: This keyboard spans C4 (261.63 Hz) to B5 (987.77 Hz) - two octaves in the middle of the piano's range. A full piano runs from A0 (27.5 Hz) to C8 (4186 Hz), but the middle octaves are where melodies live.

piano-note-checker.formula:
Note name from MIDI: name = NOTE_NAMES[midi mod 12] + (floor(midi / 12) - 1)
Frequency: f = 440 x 2^((midi - 69) / 12)
Example: C4 is MIDI 60: f = 440 x 2^(-9/12) = 261.63 Hz.

Watch your accuracy: above 80% on white keys means you are ready for black keys too.
keyFacts: Middle C (C4) is 261.63 Hz and sits at the centre of the piano's range.
Each octave has 12 notes: 7 white keys (naturals) and 5 black keys (sharps/flats).
C is always just left of the group of two black keys; F just left of the group of three.
A4 (440 Hz) is the tuning reference for the whole orchestra.
This keyboard covers C4 to B5: two octaves, MIDI notes 60 to 83.
Note names repeat every octave: every C sounds like every other C, just higher or lower.

piano-note-checker.workedExample:
Quiz round:
1. Switch to Quiz mode. A mystery note plays - say it is E4 (329.63 Hz).
2. Tap replay twice to fix the sound in your memory.
3. You click the E key. Correct - score 1/1, streak 1.
4. Next note plays: F#4. You click F. Wrong - the answer was F#4, streak resets.
5. After 10 rounds at 8/10, your accuracy is 80% - ready to include black keys.
